column1: # The EFFECT witness of every config key wz honours: the test that shows the key changing what a
# node does, and whether an upstream implementation was handed the same document first.
# Graded by scripts/lib/config_key_fixture_gate.py (its effect-witness site), which holds the key
# column to the honoured surface (HONOURED_SURFACE_PARTS) plus WZ_EXTENSION_HONOURED_KEYS, one row
# per key, and ratchets the count of keys that are not `differential` down.
# Columns: key <TAB> verdict <TAB> witness <TAB> host <TAB> upstream <TAB> observation <TAB> note.
#   differential        the same document is handed to an upstream implementation and to wz, the
#                       upstream effect is asserted first (the positive control), and wz's effect is
#                       compared with it. The one verdict that counts as proven.
#   foreign             an upstream implementation on the far side observes wz's effect, with a
#                       control on the same run, but no upstream node is handed the document.
#   wz-effect           wz's effect is observed (two documents, or with and without the key), and
#   reader-only         surveyed: only reader or expansion tests exist, nothing observes an effect.
#   unsurveyed          not yet classified; counted as unproven like the two above.
#   no-upstream-effect  a wz extension the pinned upstream parses and discards, so there is no
#                       upstream effect to compare; allowed only for WZ_EXTENSION_HONOURED_KEYS.
# witness: <path from the repository root>::<test fn> for differential, foreign and wz-effect;
#   `-` otherwise. The fn must be a test of that file, and the file must name the key or its leaf.
# host: the wz node or library the witness drives (demo, peer, router-hat, storage-host, capi-c).
# upstream: zenohd, zenoh-c or zenoh-pico for differential and foreign; `-` otherwise.
# observation: what the witness of a witnessed row observes, `-` for a row with no witness. A key
#   whose effect is not on the wire is witnessed by extending what is observed, never excused:
#   wire         the bytes a node writes on a link or a group, read off a tap or a capture;
#   delivery     what a node does as its application or a peer sees it, through an API or the
#                protocol: what is received or answered, whether an open, a link or a listener
#                comes up, what the node reports of itself;
#   resource     what a node holds of its host, read with the host's own instruments rather than
#                through zenoh: heap blocks, kernel socket state, files, mappings;
#   statistical  a distribution over repeated runs, decided by a sequential test at a stated
# note: free text, `-` when there is nothing to add.
